title: Optimization of an analytical methodology to determine microplastic contamination in different seaweed groups (Phaeophyceae, Rhodophyta and Chlorophyta)
author: Pereira, Almeida, et al.

steps.title: Prepare microplastic particles
steps.instruction: Obtain twelve polymer types (PS, AC, CA, Ly, PA, PVC, PP, PE, PET, HDPE, LDPE, RA) by manually cutting larger plastic items (fabric, bottles, fishing nets, PVC pipes, etc.), then sieve the fragments through a 5 mm mesh to discard particles larger than 5 mm; use these non‑brand‑new particles for all subsequent tests.

steps.title: Record baseline MP characteristics
steps.instruction: For each polymer, document colour, size range and visual aspect, then acquire FTIR spectra on a PerkinElmer FTIR Spectrum 2 with ATR: four scans per sample covering 400 – 4000 cm⁻¹; compare spectra to reference databases and accept identifications with confidence > 75 %.

steps.title: Wash and dry seaweed
steps.instruction: Weigh 10–15 g fresh weight of each seaweed species (F. vesiculosus, C. crispus, U. lactuca). Wash the tissue in 1 % (v/v) Triton X‑100 solution with constant mixing for 30 min. Filter the wash water through a 0.45 µm nitrate‑cellulose membrane, transfer the filter to a clean glass petri dish and dry at room temperature. Dry the washed seaweed at 60 °C for 24 h, then manually break it to homogenise.

steps.title: Create seaweed replicates
steps.instruction: From each dried seaweed batch, take three sub‑replicates of 0.5 g each and place each sub‑replicate into a separate 250 mL glass bottle (total of three replicates per condition).

steps.title: Weigh MPs into vials
steps.instruction: For each polymer, weigh 2 mg into a previously cleaned and dried 26 mL scintillation glass vial; prepare three replicates per polymer for each test (B.1 and B.2).

steps.title: Digest seaweed (cellulase then H₂O₂)
steps.instruction: Add 50 mL of 1 % (w/v) cellulase solution (0.5 g cellulase from Aspergillus niger dissolved in 50 mL 0.1 M acetate buffer, pH 5.0) to each seaweed bottle, seal and incubate at 50 °C for 24 h. Then add 100 mL of 30 % (v/v) H₂O₂, seal and incubate at 65 °C for 24, 48 or 72 h (choose the desired duration). After each incubation period, filter the entire contents through a 0.45 µm nitrate‑cellulose membrane, transfer the filter to a clean glass petri dish and dry at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Add cellulase solution and incubate 50 °C, 24 h.
Add H₂O₂ and incubate 65 °C for 24/48/72 h.
Filter through 0.45 µm membrane and dry at room temperature.

steps.title: Digest MPs (cellulase then H₂O₂)
steps.instruction: To each MP vial add 5 mL of 1 % (w/v) cellulase solution (0.05 g cellulase in 5 mL 0.1 M acetate buffer, pH 5.0) ensuring the particles are fully submerged; incubate at 50 °C for 24 h. Then add 10 mL of 30 % (v/v) H₂O₂ and incubate at 65 °C for 24, 48 or 72 h. After each incubation period, filter the suspension through a 0.45 µm nitrate‑cellulose membrane, transfer to a clean glass petri dish and dry at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Add cellulase solution and incubate 50 °C, 24 h.
Add H₂O₂ and incubate 65 °C for 24/48/72 h.
Filter through 0.45 µm membrane and dry at room temperature.

steps.title: Assess separate reagent effects (Test B.2)
steps.instruction: For polymers that showed < 90 % recovery, run two independent assays: (i) add 5 mL of 1 % (w/v) cellulase solution (0.05 g cellulase in 5 mL acetate buffer, pH 5.0) and incubate at 50 °C for 24 h; (ii) add 10 mL of 30 % (v/v) H₂O₂ and incubate at 65 °C for 72 h. After each incubation, filter through a 0.45 µm nitrate‑cellulose membrane, transfer to a clean glass petri dish and dry at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Cellulase‑only assay: add cellulase, incubate 50 °C, 24 h, then filter.
H₂O₂‑only assay: add H₂O₂, incubate 65 °C, 72 h, then filter.

steps.title: Microscopic and FTIR analysis
steps.instruction: Examine each filter under a stereomicroscope: for Test A assess completeness of seaweed tissue digestion; for Tests B.1 and B.2 evaluate any changes in MP colour, size or morphology. Weigh MPs before and after digestion (Tests B.1 and B.2) to calculate recovery rates. Perform FTIR on MPs before and after the digestion protocol using the same parameters as in step 2 to confirm polymer identity.

steps.title: Statistical analysis of results
steps.instruction: Using R, conduct a nested two‑way ANOVA with incubation duration nested within MP type to evaluate effects on recovery rates; apply post‑hoc Tukey HSD tests via the aov and TukeyHSD functions from the native stats library.
